ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: What stage in the cycle is shown at letter C?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: This is a butterfly life cycle diagram. At the top there is an adult butterfly, labeled D beside it; the letter C in the upper right position is beside a small oval, striped object, with an arrow pointing from the butterfly to this object, and continuing to point to the hatched larva/caterpillar stage. The lower and left sides of the diagram show the caterpillar continuing to grow and forming a pupa, finally returning to the adult butterfly. Reasoning: The question asks which stage in the cycle is shown by the letter C. According to the sequence of the butterfly life cycle, the adult lays eggs, the eggs hatch into caterpillars, then form pupae, and then become adults. The small oval object beside C corresponds to an egg, therefore C is the egg stage.
